spec.name: Reversal v38
spec.notes: Fade the last move, rebalanced often.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.6, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.65 to 0.14 (change -1.51). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.65 to 1.65. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is -0.43 (as submitted, 0 bps: 1.65); it breaks even at 7.9 bps with daily turnover 0.35.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.65 against 1.65 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -1.06 against 1.65 in research, a gap of +2.70.
The best year gives 19% of total P&L (year 5) and calm regimes give 71%; Sharpe is 2.0 in calm and 1.28 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 5 distinct specs; the best of 5 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.09, so the claimed 1.60 becomes 1.51 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.65 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.01, 95th percentile 0.50).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.65 to as low as 1.15 (as low as 1.52 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 35% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 20% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (cost_test EX-3, holdout_test EX-5).
